references.shows: Modern 47-string concert grand specifications and a neutral oblique photo showing the carved column, curved action plate, tapered soundbox and pedal base.
Early model 23 semi-grand record documenting the forked discs and the three left and four right pitch pedals. This historical example has different string and total pedal counts.

silhouette: Tall open concert-harp frame with a straight column, S-curved neck, slanted soundbox and low pedal base.
features: A straight fluted column with a carved crown and molded collars at the top and bottom.
An S-curved neck with a gold action plate and two rows suggesting the double-action discs.
Forty-seven strings from the neck to the soundboard, longest beside the column, with recurring red C and blue F strings.
A sloped soundbox widening toward the foot, with a separate edge and soundboard inlay.
A low molded pedal base with the four near-side pedal tips visible in three-quarter view.
iconFeatures: Tall upright open frame with a curved neck and sampled strings.
Small horizontal foot below the pillar and slanted soundbox.
avoid: A short lever harp with a bare foot
notes: The modern concert grand represents one form of the broader harp family. The historical record supports the pedal action. The maker photo guides the modern model’s anatomy and the upright playing pose.

geometry.view: Shallow three-quarter view from the action side, looking across the string plane toward the soundboard and pedal tips.
geometry.proportions: The upright column runs nearly the full height. The pictured width is just under half the height. The top of the soundbox meets the neck about one third of the way down.
geometry.partLayout: The column and steeply inclined soundbox share a molded pedal base. The neck descends from the crown and bends back up into the shoulder. Each string meets the underside of the neck and the soundboard.

documentedDimensions.value: 188 cm high, 98 cm wide, 55 cm at the broadest part of the soundboard
